findings.where: Nav bar (the binding strip), the logo lockup at top left, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The logo is recoloured. Its arches and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark are set in pale gold on the binding brown, not in the logo's own grey #404040 and blue #0070C0. It is also cut down to the mark and 'MMM INFRA', without 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services'. The palette tile never names the logo's two colours, either as tokens or as logo-only, so this look has no ground on which the logo can appear as it is.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brief says the logo stays. A returning contact who knows the blue-and-grey mark from his current site and documents may not recognise it as his.

findings.where: First screen, desktop: the 'Write to me' note in the left margin
findings.fault: The page's one action is the smallest and lightest thing in the hero. It is a short red scrawl outside the text column, left of the margin rule, beside the italic line, while the headline, the clipped print and the large aqueduct sketch take the eye. Red handwriting in a legal pad's margin also reads as a correction or an annotation, not an invitation. Nothing about it looks like a way to get in touch.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided to contact Mark. They scan the column and the nav for a contact route and either miss the margin note or fall back on 'Contact', so a contact takes more effort and some are lost.

findings.where: Hero, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The only proof on the first screen is a size word, not a checkable fact. The World Bank PPP role in the line above is the specific. This line repeats it as a boast.
findings.who_objects: Procurement staff who judge a consultant against terms of reference by named bodies, roles and regions. To them a years count reads as a firm's sales line, against the brief's 'one strong line, no boasts'.

findings.where: The contact route on the whole tile: the 'Write to me' note (mailto) and the 'Contact' nav link; the page ends on the motion sketch with no footer
findings.fault: Mark's email address never appears as text anywhere. The only direct route is a mailto hidden behind 'Write to me'. The palette says the Binding colour is for 'nav, footer', but no footer is drawn, so the look never shows where the address and the copyright date would sit.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a work machine where mailto opens nothing, or one who wants to copy the address into a procurement system. Neither can see it, and the layout round inherits no place to put it.

findings.where: Article specimen: the pull quote in Nanum Pen Script, desktop-03 and phone-02/03; also the motion-sketch heading 'written, steady, by hand'
findings.fault: The tile breaks its own rule for the hand: 'one note per view, the call to action in the margin, never body text'. On the article page the hand sets a three-to-five-line pull quote, and the desktop view of it also holds the motion-sketch heading in the same hand. On the 64 px leading the quote breaks into double-spaced lines that read like a comic aside, not a lawyer's point.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and the layout round, who will copy the article specimen as the template and spread the script into every post. Readers of a PPP article, who find the key line the hardest to read on the page.

findings.where: Article specimen heading 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', desktop-02
findings.fault: On desktop the two-line heading is set on the 64 px rule spacing at about half that size. Its lines sit a full blank rule apart and read as two separate headings. On phone the same heading is set tight. The heading treatment differs between widths, and on desktop the heading does not hold together.
findings.who_objects: Article readers, who lose the title as one unit, and the layout round, which gets two contradictory heading specs.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture link row 'Streamlining the PPP Process… / Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' (desktop-03, phone-03)
findings.fault: The row's bottom rule runs right along the baseline of the second line, under both the title and the 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' column. It looks like an underline over the whole row, so the date and the 'PDF' label also look like the link, but only the title acts. The narrow meta column breaks the date across two lines even on desktop, where there is room.
findings.who_objects: A reader looking for Mark's latest talk, who cannot tell what to click and sees the date split as '23 April / 2026'.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the 'Replay the note' button (desktop-03, phone-03/04)
findings.fault: The button is styled as an underlined text link, the look reserved for links, so it reads as navigation. On desktop it also sits two screens below the hero's margin note it replays, so a visitor who presses it sees nothing change.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, reviewing the motion principle. They press 'Replay', see no effect, and cannot judge the motion the tile proposes.

findings.where: Margin line down the left of the pad, desktop and phone, against the palette's 'Margin red #B8322B — margin, note'
findings.fault: The drawn margin is a thin dark olive-brown double line, not the red the palette names and the direction card promises. The only red on the page is the note. The tile's palette and its render disagree about the pad's most recognisable mark.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for a legal pad and knows its red margin. The layout round, which cannot tell which of the two colours is meant.

findings.where: Motion sketch timeline table on phone (phone-03)
findings.fault: At phone width the Element column narrows to one or two words a line, so the 'Hold' row runs eleven lines while the Start, Length and Easing cells stand nearly empty. The table is hard to read as a timeline.
findings.who_objects: Mark, reviewing the tile on his phone, who has to piece together what happens when.
